Anatomic Site:Brain, biopsy, recurrent, GBM, fs
Left recurrent tumor- FS
Left recurrent tumor- FS
Brain, biopsy- "NM" (FS)
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 68-year-old man with history of glioblastoma multiforme,
status post radiation and chemotherapy.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in three parts, each labeled with the patient's
name and medical record number.
Part A is additionally labeled "recurrent GBM." It consists of a single
unoriented fragment of pink-gray, soft tissue, measuring
0.5 x 0.6 x 0.4 cm. Half of this fragment is submitted for frozen section
diagnosis as FS1, with the frozen section remnant
submitted in cassette A1. The remaining unfrozen portion is submitted in
cassette A2.
Part B is additionally labeled "recurrent tumor." It consists of multiple
fragments of gray-white, soft tissue, measuring 0.7 x
1.0 x 0.4 cm in aggregate. Approximately one-fourth of the specimen is
submitted for frozen section diagnosis as FS2, with the
frozen section remnant submitted in cassette B1. The remainder of the
specimen is then submitted for frozen section diagnosis
as FS3, with the frozen section remnant submitted in cassette B2.
Part C is additionally labeled "left recurrent tumor." It consists of three
unoriented fragments of yellow-tan, soft tissue,
measuring 1.2 x 0.7 x 0.5 cm in aggregate. The specimen is entirely submitted
for frozen section diagnosis as FS4, with the
frozen section remnant submitted in cassette C1.
Diagnosis Comments:
In the biopsy submitted as Part C, approximately 75% of the tissue is necrotic
with scattered clusters of neoplastic astrocytes,
most notably on slides C2-C4. These findings support the diagnosis of
residual/recurrent glioblastoma multiforme (astrocytoma,
WHO grade IV).
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, "recurrent GBM," biopsy: Extensive necrosis with adjacent
granulation tissue, no glioblastoma identified.
Tissue section and cytologic preparation (one-third of specimen utilized).
(Dr. Lisa Chang, 60832.)
FS2 (B) Brain, "recurrent tumor," biopsy: Gray and white matter with
astrogliosis and rare atypical astrocytes; no definitive
glioblastoma. Tissue section and cytologic preparation. (Dr. Lisa Chang,
60832.)
FS3 (B) Brain, "recurrent tumor," biopsy: Gray and white matter with
astrogliosis. (Dr. Lisa Chang, 60832.)
FS4 (C) Brain, "left recurrent tumor," biopsy: Gray and white matter with
astrogliosis. (Dr. Lisa Chang, 60832.)
Final Diagnosis:
A. Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Extensive necrosis with adjacent
granulation tissue, no glioblastoma identified.
B. Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Gray and white matter with mild
astrogliosis; no glioblastoma identified.
C. Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Multifocal neoplastic astrocytes,
consistent with residual/recurrent glioblastoma
multiforme; see comment.
